citation: Sheehan, T. (2019). Heidegger: πάθος as the Thing Itself. In C. Hadjioannou (Ed.), Heidegger on Affect (Philosophers in Depth, pp. 29–46). Palgrave Macmillan. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-24639-6_2
thesis: Argues in four steps that πάθος -- read not as passing emotion but as facticity -- is die Sache selbst, 'the thing itself,' of Heidegger's entire philosophical project: (1) Heidegger's Sein-question is really about Anwesen (intelligibility) and its Herkunft; (2) transcendence is the ratio essendi of intentionality-as-'minding'; (3) an interlude shows Heidegger rendering Aristotle's own implicit phenomenology explicit; (4) facticity, read via Aristotle's dynamis tou pathein (Metaphysics IX), is what Sheehan calls 'the factum' -- the single, unitary, non-relational bond of ex-sistence and intelligibility renamed across Heidegger's career as In-der-Welt-sein, Gegenschwung, Ereignis, Seyn, Bestimmt-sein, and Bezug. Chapter authored by Thomas Sheehan; Hadjioannou is the volume editor only. Never engages Heidegger's boredom analysis (FCM) by name; engages Aristotle's De Interpretatione/De Anima/Metaphysics IX pathos-material, not the Rhetoric's persuasive pathe.

sections.title: Sense-making (Sinn, Bedeutsamkeit) as inescapable and constitutive; Sartre/Roquentin illustration; announcement of the four-step argument

The Goal -- Sein as provisional stand-in for Anwesen; the 'factum' as the single bond of ex-sistence and intelligibility; polemic against hypostasizing 'Being Itself' as a Super-Sein (Capobianco named in n.13)

Transcendence and Intentionality -- ratio essendi/ratio cognoscendi; intentionality renamed 'minding'; rejection of mind-as-container via Sartre's 'digestive epistemology'; Aristotle's De Interpretatione on the mind's pathemata; Sorge's double focus
Interlude: Phenomenology -- Aristotle's two questions of prote philosophia transposed from direct-realist to phenomenological register (to on -> to paron; ousia -> parousia)

pathos -- Heraclitus/Plato on pathos as philosophia's arche; relocation of pathos from emotion to existential Stimmung; the tuning/call-and-response risk; resolution via Bestimmt-sein/Bezug/Brauch; derivation from Aristotle's dynamis tou pathein (Metaphysics IX); closing equation pathos = facticity = the factum
Endnotes 1-41 -- German/Greek/Latin textual apparatus (GA volume-and-page citations, Grimm's dictionary, Aquinas) supporting nearly every claim

constructs.label: situational vs. trait/state boredom
constructs.treatment: analogical only (P/anticipatory-application) -- boredom is never mentioned; Sheehan's central distinction between psychological/existentiel passing affect and existential-structural facticity, plus Sorge's double focus (attuned minding of the clearing vs. relating to things within it), offers a ready-made frame for the state-vs-trait axis

readings.text: Heidegger used 'Sein' only as a provisional stand-in for Anwesen, the intelligibility/meaningful presence of whatever is encountered; the real goal of his work lay beyond Anwesen, at its Herkunft ('whence').

Intelligibility occurs only in correlation with human being; the a priori togetherness of ex-sistence and intelligibility is named across Heidegger's career as In-der-Welt-sein, Gegenschwung, Ereignis, Seyn, Entsprechung -- all naming one unitary 'factum' (SZ 53) that must never be split into two terms subsequently related.

The 'worst parody' of Heidegger's thought hypostasizes 'Being Itself' into a Super-Sein that gives/withdraws itself -- 'crude but deadly serious mythologizing'; Capobianco named (n.13) as its standard-bearer.

Transcendence is the ratio essendi of intentionality; intentionality is the ratio cognoscendi of transcendence; intentionality thereafter means only transcendence-based intentionality, termed 'minding.'

There is no 'inside' to ex-sistence; we are always already 'outside' (Draussensein, SZ 62), and this outsideness is our condition of being inside meaning -- against Sartre's 'digestive epistemology' parody.

Aristotle's De Interpretatione (16a6-8): the mind has pathemata (impressions), rendered Erlebnisse by Heidegger; these are 'likenesses' (homoiomata) of things, not inner images, but the mode of assimilation to what is directly, meaningfully present.

Sorge has a double focus: attuned minding of the clearing (befindliches Verstehen/verstehende Befindlichkeit) and relating to things within it (Sein bei); existentielly Besorgen/Fuersorge/Selbstsorge, existentially In-der-Welt-sein/Jemeinigkeit/Seinkoennen.

Aristotle's two questions of prote philosophia (ti to on hei on; tis he ousia), posed direct-realistically (exo kai choriston), are transposed phenomenologically: to on becomes to paron, ousia becomes parousia -- rendering explicit, not imposing on, Aristotle's own convertibility of on and alethes.

In the 1955 lecture 'What Is Philosophy?' (GA 11:7-26), Heidegger says philosophy's basic factum must concern us personally and touch us at the root of our existence, raising (without settling) the worry that philosophy is then a matter of feeling; tested against Gide's 'fine sentiments make for bad literature.'

Via Heraclitus (fr. 35, 50, 51), the pre-Platonic philosophos is one already attuned to/in harmony (homologein, harmonie) with logos, not one who strives (orexis/eros) for sophia; by Plato/Aristotle's time this attunement had devolved into striving for wisdom.

Plato's Theaetetus (155d2-4): Socrates names pathos -- wondering/marveling -- as the sole arche of philosophy; arche names both origin and sustaining principle, so wonder maintains philosophy throughout, not merely starts it.

Heidegger relocates pathos out of psychological/existentiel emotion into the existential structure Stimmung (attunement to Seyn) -- repeating the move already made with Befindlichkeit at SZ section 29.

The 'tuning' (stimmen) and 'call-and-response' (Stimme und Zuspruch des Seyns) images for Stimmung risk reinstating a two-term, subject-object structure -- the same crypto-metaphysical Super-Seyn error Step 1 ruled out.

Resolution via Bestimmt-sein (Grimm: bestimmen = constituere/kathistemi, causative): (i) the achieved, fulfilled state of ex-sistence brought to its telos, not cessation; (ii) a reinscription of the same factum earlier called Geworfenheit, later Ereignet-sein; (iii) no agent throws/appropriates/attunes ex-sistence ab extra as an efficient cause (poietikon) acts on a patient (pathetikon) -- yet pathos remains at the heart of the project, now naming this existential structure itself.

Via 'Conversation with a Japanese Professor' (GA 12:119): the hermeneutical Bezug of ex-sistence and Sprache (= Heraclitean logos) is emphatically not a two-sided Dasein<->Seyn relation, but our fate of being 'used'/'needed' (gebraucht), belonging to a Brauch that claims us -- a one-sided fact: without us, no in-break (Einbruch), no clearing, no meaning.

Culminating thesis: Heidegger derives thrownness/appropriation/Bestimmtsein from Aristotle's dynamis tou pathein (Metaphysics IX, cf. V.12) -- pathos as a thing's passivity/receptivity, the ability to undergo or bear up under an action (poiesis). Aristotle's doctrine concerns the being of things generally; Heidegger radically adapts it to human being's own structure: we have always already 'suffered' thrown-openness, with no prior agent forcing it on us. Therefore pathos is our facticity, and our facticity is itself the factum -- die Sache selbst of Heidegger's entire project.

concepts.gloss: intelligibility or meaningful presence; what 'Sein' was always a provisional stand-in for
Sheehan's own umbrella term for the single, unitary, non-relational bond of ex-sistence and intelligibility, renamed across Heidegger's career
ex-sistence insofar as it has always already been appropriated (via Eignung, Heidegger's translation of dynamis) to its proper status as the field of intelligibility
reciprocal sameness / back-and-forth-ness of Da-sein and Da-sein; Heidegger's 1930s name for the bond of ex-sistence and intelligibility
Sheehan's rendering of transcendence-based intentionality; covers theoretical cognition and ordinary senses ('mind the gap')
mental 'affections'/impressions (De Interpretatione 1); rendered Erlebnisse by Heidegger; likenesses (homoiomata), not inner images
care/concern/interest; double focus on the field of meaning (attunement+understanding) and on things within it (Sein bei)
ex-sistence's achieved, fulfilled condition of having been de-fined/de-termined to its telos; reinscribes Geworfenheit/Ereignet-sein
the hermeneutical 'relation' of ex-sistence and Sprache (Heraclitean logos); explicitly not a two-sided Dasein<->Seyn relation
our fate of being needed/used (gebraucht) to sustain and be the clearing; the one-sided existential fact grounding Bezug

a thing's passivity/receptivity -- the ability to undergo, receive, or bear up under an action (poiesis); Aristotle's general ontological doctrine (Metaphysics IX, V.12), radically adapted by Heidegger to name ex-sistence's own facticity
both origin and sustaining principle; wonder (pathos) as arche of philosophy does not merely start it but maintains it throughout

interlocutors.name: Martin Heidegger
interlocutors.role: primary text under analysis across GA 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 58, 60, 61, 64, 73, 78, 83, and Sein und Zeit; also the 1955 'What Is Philosophy?' (GA 11) and 'Conversation with a Japanese Professor' (GA 12)

interlocutors.name: Aristotle
interlocutors.role: source of the mind's pathemata (De Interpretatione 1), the soul as 'somehow all things' (De Anima III.8), the two questions of prote philosophia and convertibility of on/alethes (Metaphysics IV, VII, I), and dynamis tou pathein (Metaphysics IX, V.12) -- the ultimate textual source Heidegger radically adapts for facticity-as-pathos

interlocutors.name: Plato
interlocutors.role: Theaetetus 155d2-4: Socrates names pathos (wondering/marveling) as the sole arche of philosophy; also Republic 509b9 (epekeina tes ousias) and Theaetetus 176b1 (homoiosis theoi)

interlocutors.name: Heraclitus
interlocutors.role: fragments 35, 50, 51: philosophos as attuned-to/in-harmony-with logos (homologein, harmonie), prior to the later devolution into striving for sophia

interlocutors.name: Richard Capobianco
interlocutors.role: named (n.13) as the standard-bearer of the 'Super-Sein' mythologizing reading Sheehan rejects -- Being Itself as a hypostasized Metaphysical Something that gives/withdraws itself

interlocutors.name: Jean-Paul Sartre
interlocutors.role: source of the 'digestive epistemology' parody of mind-as-container (rejected as a model), and of the Nausea/crabs anecdote illustrating inescapable sense-making even when 'getting it wrong'

interlocutors.name: Thomas Aquinas
interlocutors.role: cited via Heidegger's SZ for the soul as ens quod natum est convenire cum omni ente (nature of the soul is to 'come together' with all things)

interlocutors.name: Andre Gide
interlocutors.role: 'fine sentiments make for bad literature,' invoked and provisionally tested against philosophy in the discussion of whether philosophy is a matter of pathos/feeling

tensions.label: Correlational vs. hypostasized Being
tensions.poles: Sheehan's own non-metaphysical, correlational reading of Ereignis/Seyn as inseparable from ex-sistence vs. Capobianco-style readings that treat 'Being Itself' as an independent Super-Sein that gives, withdraws, and hides itself

tensions.label: Pathos as psychological emotion vs. existential-structural facticity
tensions.poles: the surface/ordinary reading of pathos as a passing feeling or passion (invited by Plato's 'wondering' and the 1955 lecture's 'touches us deeply') vs. Heidegger's/Sheehan's relocation of pathos into Stimmung as an existential structure equivalent to Geworfenheit/Ereignetsein

tensions.label: Relational (two-term) vs. one-sided Stimmung
tensions.poles: the 'tuning' (stimmen)/'call-and-response' (Stimme und Zuspruch des Seyns) imagery, which risks a two-term subject-object structure, vs. Bestimmt-sein/Bezug/Brauch, which resolve the risk via a strictly one-sided, non-relational factum

tensions.label: Ontological/psychological pathos (this chapter) vs. rhetorical pathe (Rhetoric II)
tensions.poles: Sheehan's engagement with pathos exclusively via De Interpretatione's mental pathemata and Metaphysics IX's dynamis tou pathein (a being's general capacity to be acted upon) vs. the Rhetoric's taxonomy of audience-directed persuasive emotions (anger, fear, pity, etc.) -- an adjacent but textually distinct lineage of the same Greek root pascho, never bridged by Sheehan himself
tensions.locus: p.34-35; 42-43 (P/anticipatory-application -- our own observation, not the chapter's claim)
